title: Description
description: What a vulnerability database holds for one vulnerability, from each of its providers, and whether each package that it was asked about has the fix of a provider. The strings are the database's own.

vulnerabilityID.description: The ID that the database was asked about.

aliases.description: The IDs of the same vulnerability that the records name, such as the CVE of a GitHub advisory, sorted.

cvss.description: The vectors of the records' scores, each once.

knownExploited.description: True when a record lists the vulnerability as known to be exploited.

epssPermille.description: The EPSS score of the vulnerability's CVE in per mille: floor(score x 1000). Left out where the database has none.

epssDate.description: The date of the EPSS score.

references.description: The URLs that the records name, each once.

packages.description: The packages that the database was asked about, as they were given.

providers.description: What each provider says of a fix: the entries that answer for an asked package, and for a package that none answers for, some that name it. Empty when there are none.

otherProviders.description: The entries that the list of providers leaves out, counted per provider, sorted by provider. Each says Unknown for every asked package.

version.description: The version of CVSS, such as 3.1.

type.description: Syft's type of the package, such as deb, rpm, apk or go-module.

purl.description: The purl, which names the source package in the qualifier upstream and the release in distro.

distro.description: The distribution and its release, such as debian-12, where the purl names none, and the purl's where it does.

vulnerabilityID.description: The ID of the vulnerability whose records the answer rests on: the ID asked about, or one that its records name.

namespace.description: Grype's namespace, such as debian:distro:debian:12 or github:language:go.

package.description: The name of the package that the provider lists, or the CPE that NVD lists.

fixState.description: Grype's: fixed when the provider names a fix, else not-fixed, wont-fix or not-affected. Empty when the provider says nothing.

packages.description: The answer for each asked package.

fixedForInstalled.description: Yes: the provider speaks for the package's distribution or ecosystem, no range that it lists holds the installed version, and the installed version is at a fixed version or above. No: such a provider lists a range that holds it. Unknown: anything else.
